In [[mathematics]], a '''Frink ideal''', introduced by [[Orrin Frink]], is a certain kind of subset of a [[partially ordered set]].

== Basic definitions ==

LU(''A'') is the set of all common [[lower bound]]s of the set of all common [[upper bound]]s of the subset ''A'' of a [[partially ordered set]].

A  subset ''I'' of a partially ordered set (''P'',&nbsp;≤) is a '''Frink ideal''', if the following condition holds:

For every finite subset ''S'' of ''I'', we have LU(''S'')&nbsp;<math>\subseteq</math>&nbsp;''I''.

A  subset ''I'' of a partially ordered set (''P'',&nbsp;≤) is a '''normal ideal''' or a '''cut''' if LU(''I'')&nbsp;<math>\subseteq</math>&nbsp;''I''.

== Remarks==

#Every Frink ideal ''I'' is a [[lower set]].
#A subset ''I'' of a [[lattice (order)|lattice]] (''P'',&nbsp;≤) is a  Frink ideal [[if and only if]] it is a lower set that is closed under finite joins ([[suprema]]).
# Every normal ideal is a Frink ideal.
